# Non-functional requirements

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*


#### Non-functional requirements

Answered directly by Stephen, none inferred from the design material.

| NFR | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Security | **Access control is specified once, as acceptance criteria in F7, and is not restated here** — no sign-up, no passwords, single-use emailed codes with an invisible rate limit, a sliding thirty-day session revocable from the account sheet, row-level isolation from the first migration, and no FPL credentials ever requested, stored or transmitted. What is genuinely non-functional and therefore lives here: **AI and data-provider keys are server-side only and are never present in anything the browser downloads** — not in a bundle, not in an environment variable exposed to the client, not in a network response. This is the one security requirement that no screen or flow expresses, so nothing else in the document can catch it being broken. |
| Cost control | **This is the single home for the spend cap; 2.2, 2.5 and F7 point here rather than restate it.** **Two layers:** a £50 prepaid balance in the AI provider's console, set up from the first commit, as the hard cap; and the refresh design's evidence check, which already avoids the call entirely when nothing has changed, so most weeks barely touch the balance. A third layer — a per-user daily ceiling in application code — is deliberately not built: the safeguard stays external and simple. The prepaid cap fails hard, not gracefully — when it's exhausted the app is dead until Stephen tops it up or decides otherwise — which is accepted for a personal, single-user build: the likeliest cause of a runaway bill is a retry loop, not a stranger, and any trip is something Stephen will see and handle himself. |
| Performance | Cold open to a responsive screen in three seconds or less — in practice the Thinking state, since every route that re-reads the world passes through it; the squad itself then lands within the advice-run budget below. **A full advice generation in sixty seconds or less at the 95th percentile.** That is a deliberately loose starting budget, not a target: the pipeline makes a candidate-proposal call, a judgement call per player involved and a separate reasoning call per call produced, and nobody has measured it yet. It is set wide enough that the first real run is a measurement rather than a failure, and it is expected to come down once there are numbers — a refresh that finds no new evidence does not call the model at all (F6-RS-08) and should land far inside it. Because a minute is long enough to feel broken, the Thinking state carries the weight: it states an expected duration honestly rather than a fixed figure, narrates real progress throughout (F6-AC-17, F6-AC-18), and stays cancellable for the whole budget (F6-AC-19). Any non-AI interaction — tab switch, filter, swipe decision, scroll — responds within 200 milliseconds. Recomputation after a candidate swap is local and immediate. |
| Scalability | None, explicitly. One manager, one FPL team, one active session. There is no load, concurrency or growth target; the only ceiling that matters is the AI spend cap. Serving more people would be a rewrite, not a scaling exercise. |
| Accessibility | No formal WCAG conformance target for a single-user app. Four requirements instead, all of them settled in the Design System before the build prompt rather than patched after. **(1) Sizes.** Primary interactive targets stay at 44 points and the stated minimum type sizes hold. **(2) Contrast, on all small text and not only body copy.** Every piece of text below the large-text threshold meets 4.5:1 — secondary text, column headers, team tags and metadata included. Three measured failures in the current design material are forbidden by this and need token changes: the muted secondary colour `#847F74` on `#EDE8DE` at 3.26:1 and `#8A857B` on white at 3.67:1, used for almost every column header, team tag and metadata string across the stat table, the candidate list and the squad cards; and the accent green `#10985A` on `#EDE8DE` at 3.04:1, used for positive numeric values such as xPts deltas. The darker `#0A6E3D` passes at 5.19:1 and is the substitution for the green; the muted pair needs a darkened token of its own. These are two token changes, not nineteen screen fixes. **(3) No state by colour alone.** Specifically the chip discs' available-versus-spent state and the chip-plan timeline's recommended-versus-possible-week distinction (F5); the conviction band already carries its band word alongside the figure and satisfies this. **(4) A visible focus state on every interactive element.** The design material is a static export and shows no hover, focus or pressed state anywhere, so none can be assumed to exist. |
| Reliability | No uptime target. Instead, four hard requirements: a failed run never destroys existing advice or decisions; the last-run time always reflects the last successful run; when FPL's feed is unreachable the app works from the last read and states how old it is; and the app never writes to FPL under any circumstance. |
